newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Consultation ends for HK broker commission changes.
newsitem.headline: Consultation ends for HK broker commission changes.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said it had received more than 60 replies to a consultation paper on brokerage commissions ahead of Monday's deadline to respond to the proposals.
"We have had more than 60 submissions," a spokesman said, adding that the exchange was unable to say when it would report its findings.
The paper, part of a review of transaction costs in Hong Kong, was sent to more than 500 brokerage firms.
Brokerage firms were asked to consider adopting a negotiable commission system for orders above HK$3 million, HK$5 million or HK$7 million or retaining the current flat rate system.
"Once feedback on this consultation paper has been received, the exchange will incorporate the comments into a proposal to the government," the exchange said in the paper.
The exchange asked the government last year to reduce the stamp duty on transactions to make Hong Kong more competitive.
The government replied it needed a commitment from brokers that they would cut brokerage commissions before it considered a reduction in the stamp duty.
